Q: Application based cms or package for laravel A:

October is pretty much amazing. I think you can do anything with it. When I saw their website the first time on a recommendation of a friend I also saw it as a simple CMS - but look at the documentation- and resources-page: You can create your own plugins, it has a very intricate and easy to understand databse-handling that also manages complicated relationships like "many to many polymorphic" and there is an easy way to create backend-pages that contain forms with those relations. In my opinion its really amazingly thought through and it can serve as CMS-part for almost anything.

Q: Unable to create a Next.js app with Bun, tsconfig.json error A:

I looked it up and If you're using Bun to create a Next.js app on Windows, you might run into an annoying ENOENT error. This happens because Bun tries to read files before Windows has fully written them to disk—basically, it’s moving too fast for the file system to keep up! So Instead of creating the app through bun, try it with react and then switch to bun.

npx create-next-app@latest my-app

//then do this
cd my-app
bun install    
bun dev

Q: How can I replace a PostgreSQL materialized view definition when other objects depend on it? A:

Is DROP ... CASCADE followed by recreating the materialized view and all dependent objects the only correct approach, or is there a safer way to preserve or migrate dependencies?

Yes. Good news is, support for in-place matview redefinition is being added:

  • Add OR REPLACE option to CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW

You can follow the discussion here but it looks like it's arriving no sooner than PostgreSQL version 20 (as of writing this, we're at v19beta3).

Since you do have to rebuild objects that depend on your target materialized view, you could add an element to simplify the process later, by hiding the materialized view behind a regular view, which already supports create or replace syntax:
demo at db<>fiddle

create view v_order_summary as select*from order_summary;
create or replace view public.customer_report AS
SELECT
    customer_id,
    order_count
--dependencies should point at the view, not the underlying matview:
FROM public.v_order_summary
WHERE order_count > 0;

That allows you to do a sort of Indiana Jones idol swap whenever you need to redefine the matview:

begin transaction;

alter materialized view public.order_summary rename to order_summary_old;

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW public.order_summary AS
SELECT
    customer_id,
    count(*) AS order_count,
    sum(amount) AS total_amount--new column
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id;

create or replace view v_order_summary as --redirect intermediate view to new matview
  select*from public.order_summary;

refresh materialized view public.order_summary_old with no data;--clear old matview

commit;

It's a minor quality-of-life addition and not really a workaround - you still need to redefine dependencies but now you're limiting them to a single one and everything else downstream from the intermediate view can remain blissfully unaware of the change.

Both this and the upcoming syntax will work fine for querying that directly or adding new objects referencing the newly added column, or manually altering existing ones to add it in.

Neither that nor the upcoming syntax is meant for cascading the change through dependencies that you defined using select * or table - those aren't dynamic:

create view v2 as select * from public.v_order_summary;
create view v3 as table v2;
select pg_get_viewdef('v2'),  pg_get_viewdef('v3');
pg_get_viewdef pg_get_viewdef
SELECT customer_id,
    order_count,
    total_amount
   FROM v_order_summary;		 SELECT customer_id,
    order_count,
    total_amount
   FROM v2;

Since this only works if you're writing new queries and defining new objects that include the new column reference, you could just as well add a matview on top of your matview, and point to the new one wherever you need the added column.

Avoiding that is understandable because this would mean you'd have to somehow sync up the refresh schedules of both matviews (there's no refresh..cascade to avoid stale inputs, and regular refresh uses upstream content, rather than definitions).

It would also be more expensive to refresh them independently - in a single matview, you can collect count(*) and sum(amount) in a single scan. With two separate ones, they're scanning the sources twice, then the new one needs to join the results.

Q: Oracle dataguard is not working properly because a FAL[client] A:

This question is 5 years old but I feel it hasn't been completely answered yet.

First how does oracle resolves the gap:

The MRP process is the one triggering the request for a GAP. That process is turned on like so: Without standby redo logs: alter database recover managed standby database disconnect; With standby redo: alter database recover managed standby database using current logfile disconnect;

If you have only one standby database for your primary database, then fal_server and fal_client parameters actually don't need to be configured.

If the fal_server is missing, oracle will grab that information from log_archive_dest_n.

This means that log_archive_dest_2 needs to be configured also on the standby database.

So how to solve a GAP resolution issue:

  1. Make sure log_archive_dest_n is setup in both primary and standby
  2. Make sure that there's no typo in the "service" value of log_archive_dest_n.
  3. Make sure that the service value references a valid tns entry in tnsnames.ora
  4. Make sure that the same password file is used on all nodes of your primary and standby cluster.
  5. Make sure you can connect with sqlplus "sys/syspassword@primary as sysdba" and sqlplus "sys/syspassword@standby as sysdba" from both primary and standby.List item

The MRP process sends a GAP resolution requests every so often. If you want to get it immediately in order to make sure it works: SQL>alter database recover managed standby database cancel; SQL>alter database recover managed standby database using current logfile; (use standby redo logs, it applies logs faster on standby)

fal_server and fal_client parameters actually exists if you want to setup a cascaded standby setup.

Primary DB A sends archived logs to standby B If standby B becomes primary then send archived logs to standby C.

FAL behavior on 11.2 (Doc ID 1394472.1)

From 11.2 no need to mention FAL_CLIENT primary will take it from log_archive_dest_n (remote destination standby from where it received the FAL request) service.

FAL_SERVER And FAL_CLIENT Settings For Cascaded Standby (Doc ID 358767.1)
